examples.question: Some people believe that professionals, such as doctors and engineers, should be requierd to work in the country where they did their training. Others believe they should be free to work in another country if they wish. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
examples.essay:
There is no denying the fact that many good employees like engineers, doctor, or even scientists sometimes they prefer to get a work in foreign country or country that they do not learn in it. While it is a commonly held belief that they should work in the same place they train in it. There is also an argument that they should feel free to choose the country. This essay will analyse the topics from both points of view and give my opinion.

On one hand, working in your country is considered a social resposibility. In other words, professionals people form a important part of society, so they have to work for them to develop their countries and contribute to making thir life better.Also, there is a saying say the closer people have the right to give them your best. In addition, applying them to choose thir place work might be a problem in the feature. For example, some foreign countries give more to them, so they will use to have a high salary, which lead to increase the rate of salaries.

On the other hand, if we do not give them the right to select, it will be unfair for them and violation of rights. It is also possible to say that people always have different dreams and ambitions, so we have to respect their desires and goals even if it do not serve us. Moreover, working in different areas will give them experience and enhancing their skills

In conclusion, there is no easy anwers for this question. On balance, however, I tend to believe that professionals and talented citizens should give their effort to serve their country.

examples.question: Some people believe that professionals such as doctors and engineers, should be required to wok in the country where they did their training. Others believe they should be free to work in another country if they wish.
examples.essay:
Some people argue that experts should be made mandatory to build their careers in the nations where they trained, whereas others say that it is their freedom to work in any country they wish. While having them work in the country of training could be an immediate solution for local needs, I believe letting them work in other countries may bring more advantages

On the one hand, requiring these experts to stay after training might solve local issues immediately. This is because their training modules and case studies most likely have been adjusted to situations in the countries, like specific health problems or technological needs. Take Malaria disease, for example, and most of the sufferers are in tropical nations such as Indonesia and some others in Southeast Asia. Therefore, medical treatment obviously can be done solely in those countries. Nevertheless, mandating them could also limit their chances for career development and explore diverse practices in their respective fields.

On the other hand, there are many cases where professionals manage to establish cooperation between the foreign entities they are working for and institutions from the countries of training. These occasions bring numerous benefits for both parties, such as labour enhancement, the invention of new technology and positive economic development. For example, many Indonesian experts are sent to Japan to address the issue of labour shortage, and years later, they are involved in bilateral cooperation between both countries in the field of engineering and renewable energy. However, one drawback is that overseas companies might reject the collaboration proposals due to unmatched objectives.

In conclusion, the best way for bigger merits is by allowing professionals to work in foreign countries so that they are able to advance their careers and create more experts through labour trainings from international collaboration.

examples.question: some people believe that it is good to share as much information as possible in scientific research, business and the academic world. Others believe that some infomation is too important or too valueable to be shared freely.
examples.essay:
Although it is sometimes thought that sharing as much data as possible in the field of scientific research, business and academy are beneficial. However, other people believe that the information is too important to be shared freely. I consider that sharing valuable information as free can bring detrimental impacts to economic policies. 

On the one hand, many people think that sharing information ought to be free. Furthermore, it can help all people regardless of their background, whether rich or poor, to increase their knowledge and broaden their horizons. In other words, some free data can make it easier for people to become aware of other aspects of their lives, such as medicine or technology. For instance, all the time of the outbreak of the Covid-19 virus, which was a common issue for all countries, it was very important to report the disease in a fraction of a minute and inform all people about the consequences that they will be faced. 

On the other hand, it is sometimes believed that the principal issue with sharing valuable information  bring some damage to technology trades. Doing this means, they can not have a huge income and also benefit from the applications made. For example, the Apple company decided to make some payments Pro version of an application that people used to access information. Thus, they are forced to pay money to have access to the software. Eventually, with this ,politics the cost of building free software that is used to inform the public will be recouped.

In conclusion, while people may vary in their opinions, I think it is not essential that all information be available to the public. Although, some important data must be to prevent irreversible damage for people might face.

examples.question: Some countries have introduced laws to limit working hours for employees. Why are these laws introduced? Do you think they are a positive or negative development?
examples.essay:
Globally, many countries have put an upper cap on the number of working hours for their employees. These laws have been introduced primarily to avoid their exploitation by their employers. This is a positive development as it helps in maintaining a work-life balance, and the employee can utilise the extra time available for further skill enhancement.

To begin with, restricting the number of hours at the office safeguards the professionals from being exploited by the organisation. Managers frequently burden their subordinates with assignments that require extra time to be devoted at the workplace. However, the company does not provide any financial incentive to its junior workforce in such a scenario. Therefore, it becomes imperative that key regulations regarding an upper limit on the number of hours at work are brought in by the government. For instance, in India, the government has made mandatory, an 8-hour shift for the blue-collared employees to protect them from being exploited.

One of the key benefits of implementing such a law is that it helps an employee devote time to its family. Another benefit to consider is that it provides the workers with the flexibility to utilise the available hours to hone their skill further. People working in corporates have a family to look after to and therefore, it becomes essential that they get enough time after their job to fulfil those needs. Moreover, employees can make use of the additional time to learn something new in order to stay competitive and subsequently productive at the workplace. To illustrate, many organisations are providing incentives to their employees who want to upgrade their skillset. In addition to that, they are being offered additional paid holidays so that they feel reinvigorated with their loved ones. Thus, in my opinion, restricting working hours is a positive trend as it helps an employee maintain work-life balance and gives him an opportunity to learn something novel.

To conclude, many nations are increasingly limiting the amount of time spent at office for their workers. This is required as it protects them from being mishandled by the company. I strongly agree that this is a positive development since it allows the workers to upgrade their skillset and stay competitive. In addition to that, they gain peace of mind by devoting time to their family.

examples.question: It is now possible for scientists and tourists to travel to remote natural environment, such as South pole. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
examples.essay:
With the ever-evolving technology and easily accessible travel, people are now able to visit unexplored locations such as the South pole. In this essay, we will examine some advantages and disadvantages and draw a logical conclusion.

The two main advantages of being able to travel to remote locations are scientific advancements and potential tourist hubs. 

In other words, scientists have been exploring and researching all the geographic locations in search of answers across various fields such as geology, archaeology, medicine and ecology. For instance, the provision to explore a less-frequented environment could open doors to many new studies and help researchers discover many more new species of flora and fauna.

Similarly, tourists are always looking forward to what this exquisite planet has to offer in terms of its beauty. For example, being able to tour an extreme weathered Iceland has given an economic boost to the tourism sector across the globe with over thousands visiting the country annually today.

However, there are disadvantages to this as well such as exploitation of the habitat and pollution.

Scientists may exploit the resources of the land in the name of research. Thereafter, animals will be captured to serve as lab rats and underground holes will be dug resulting in possible over-usage of the natural resources and destruction of the wild habitat. For instance, the dense amazon forest has only a third left of it, being subjected to research, mining, deforestation and excavation.

Furthermore, tourists frequenting the place will eventually lead to littering and overcrowding. For example, the river Ganga attracts millions of people annually across the world. However, due to heavy littering and pollution, the aquatic ecosystem is destroyed and the river has now been rendered toxic for human use.

To conclude, while an unexplored land may have a lot to offer in terms of resources, science and aesthetics, I strongly opine that some places should be treasured with limited human interference and therefore believe that, the drawbacks outweigh the advantages.
